name: Instruments
plan: CANDIDATE 1: buy RIC shares the day before a capital gain dividend (day 129), sell and rebuy on the ex-date (day 130, wash sale), sell the replacement shares on day 162; dividend long-term (s.852(b)(3)(B)), loss short-term because s.852(b)(4)(A) reaches only 'such share' and s.1091(d) moves the disallowed loss into the basis of shares that received no dividend
claimed_gain: $1,768 per $10,000 of dividend (future value at 4%; $1,700 in year-1 dollars), against the plain plan

tests.detail: Every step matches the words of ss.852(b)(3)(B), 852(b)(4)(A),(C), 246(c)(3), 1091(a),(d), 1223(3); divergences found are off the plan's path or against the taxpayer, and the plan survives the strict copy and two forms without a same-day round trip.
Adding '(or of any stock or securities the basis of which is determined under section 1091(d) by reference to such share)' to s.852(b)(4)(A) removes the plan and moves no baseline.

Removing s.1091(a), s.1091(d), s.852(b)(3)(B), 'buy GainFund', 'sell GainFund' or 'sell FundA' each kills it; s.1223(3) tacking, 'buy FundA' and the same-day second lot are decoration; with all 11 unused kinds of trade removed it is still found at the same figure.
No recent amendment is involved; under the pre-1984 'less than 31 days' text a plain 33-day holding already gives the same figure, so the wash sale only undoes the 1984 lengthening.
Over every final position recognized income is never below the pre-tax result (no double deduction, no vanished income); the model only ever destroys loss (24 positions, +10,000).

Plan, baseline and closed-gap result replayed on the full rules by decide +kernel; in a cut-down model (one share class, no calendar) a theorem by induction over all move lists shows no short-term loss under the closed rule; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.
Python from the statute gives baseline 42,806, plan 41,038, saving 1,768 (1,700 before interest), identical to the Lean; holding 201 days gives the identical saving.

Regulations 1.852-4, 1.1091-1, 1.1091-2, 1.1223-1 and Publication 550 retrieved and silent on the interaction, nothing found describing it, but committee reports and the paywalled secondary literature were not reached.

divergences: Against the taxpayer: a loss sale within 30 days of the purchase of an earlier lot that is already sold is disallowed and the loss vanishes (the day-162 exit was placed to clear this; the statute needs only more than 30 days after the replacement purchase)
s.852(b)(4)(C)(ii) (days more than 6 months after the ex-date not counted) not encoded; not on the plan's path
s.246(c)(4)(A),(B) (options, contracts to sell) not encoded; no such instruments in the model
'6 months' encoded as 183 days; plan unchanged at 181, 184, 200, 201
Wash-sale matching takes the most recent acquisition; Reg. 1.1091-1(d) says the earliest; plan unchanged when fixed
s.7701(o) and step transaction not encoded; a disregarded same-day sale and repurchase gives the closed-gap result ($0)
Scenario, not rules: date grid 129/130/131/162 built around the plan; FundA leaves at exactly zero gain; all funds have identical returns so 'different fund for a day' changes nothing in the model
s.1223(3) is listed among the provisions combined but is decoration (ablation leaves $1,768)
Displayed plan among tied families depends on hash order; the original output never printed the day-162 exit

authority.quote: The rules contained in section 246(c)(3) (relating to the determination of holding periods for purposes of the deduction for dividends received) shall be applied in determining whether, for purposes of section 852(b)(4) and this paragraph, a share of regulated investment company stock has been held for a period of less than 31 days.

The acquisition of any share of stock or any security which results in the nondeductibility of a loss under the provisions of this section shall be disregarded in determining the deductibility of any other loss.
No loss from the sale is recognized under section 1091. The basis of the new share is $110; that is, the basis of the old share ($100) increased by $10
the holding period of the newly acquired securities shall include the period for which the taxpayer held the securities with respect to which the loss was not allowable.

If the disposition of a loss position would (but for the application of this section) result in a capital loss, the loss allowed under paragraph (b) of this section with respect to the disposition of the loss position shall be treated as a capital loss.

authority.source: IRS Publication 550 (2025), Holding Period and Wash Sales
authority.quote: This adjustment postpones the loss deduction until the disposition of the new stock or securities. Your holding period for the new stock or securities includes the holding period of the stock or securities sold.

authority.source: State Farm, Buying the Dividend or Capital Gain Distribution and Wash Sales
authority.quote: Your holding period for the replacement shares is also changed to include the amount of time you held the original shares.

authority.source: Journal of Accountancy, March 2003, mutual fund redemptions
authority.quote: The wash sale rule disallows a capital loss on the sale of shares to the extent the investor buys

verdict_reason: Every step is what ss.852(b)(4)(A), 1091(a),(d) and 1223(3) say, a one-phrase amendment removes it without moving any baseline, ablation and kernel replay confirm the mechanism, and no regulation or publication retrieved addresses it; but it saves nothing beyond the known six-month hold (both $1,768), was a hand-written check line rather than a printed search result, and depends on a same-price sale and repurchase being respected.
